quotes: "However, these tools focus on quantitative data, which often do not capture the deeper, contextual aspects of viewer behavior, such as motivations or preferences." (p. 2)

"The Proxona interface consists of two parts: 1) Exploration Page for exploring the audience personas by interacting with them (Figure 2), and 2) Creation Page for drafting a storyline for the video and refining it with persona feedback (Figure 3)." (p. 5)

(p. 10)

(p. 16)

"Still, in terms of making the personas feel like real individuals (Q2), the Baseline method outperformed Proxona, with evaluators feeling that Baseline personas seemed more like real viewers." (p. 12)

"However, some participants (P9, P10) found interacting with multiple personas overwhelming, noting that the diverse opinions presented by different personas made it difficult to process and synthesize feedback." (p. 14)
"Results showed that 4.93% (10 out of 203) of the responses were classified as hallucinations by at least one evaluator (IRR = 0.804)." (p. 12)

The within-subject practitioner study supports the claim for early-stage sensemaking and storyline work, but not prediction of real audience behavior or measurable engagement outcomes (PDF p. 18).

paper_code_entries.value: YouTube audience sensemaking and video-storyline ideation — the evaluated task combined audience exploration with drafting a tailored storyline (PDF p. 12).
quotes: "The task for both conditions was identical: “Begin by exploring your audience using [your existing methods / Proxona], and then develop a video storyline for the provided topic, tailored to your audience.”" (p. 12)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — Proxona supports present audience exploration, sensemaking, and ideation rather than instruction or skill development (PDF p. 18).
quotes: "While Proxona is designed for audience exploration, sensemaking and ideation, we found that participants utilized the natural language chat for purposes beyond the initial goals due to its flexibility (Section 6.6.1)." (p. 18)

quotes: "Channel activity varied from 1 year to over 6 years (See Table 1)." (p. 13)
"Four participants were full-time creators, and seven were part-time." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: knowledge_or_concept_gap — existing analytics exposed activity but not the audience motivations and preferences needed for targeting content (PDF p. 4).
quotes: "However, they found these tools provided only surface-level data, leaving them uncertain about the deeper motivations, such as why certain content resonated with their audience or what specific topics they found engaging." (p. 4)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study measured audience exploration, sensemaking, and early-stage ideation support (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "In both conditions, participants completed a questionnaire assessing the system’s usability in audience exploration, sensemaking, and early-stage ideation support (7-point Likert scale; Appendix D.1 - Table 10)." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — participants rated storylines made with Proxona as more complete (PDF p. 16).
quotes: "They also felt that a storyline created using Proxona was more complete (Q8: 𝑀𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑥𝑜𝑛𝑎 = 86.82, 𝑀𝑑𝑜𝑐𝑠 = 73.00 on a 100-point scale, p < .01) and able to plan videos with enough evidence (Q4: 𝑀𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑥𝑜𝑛𝑎 = 5.73, 𝑀𝑑𝑜𝑐𝑠 = 4.55, p < .05)." (p. 16)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the dimension–value framework organizes unstructured audience data into meaningful categories (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "This framework helps capture the detailed traits of different audience segments by organizing unstructured audience data into meaningful categories." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — the representations confront creators with audience heterogeneity and segments they had not considered (PDF p. 14).
quotes: "Participants found that Proxona helped them recognize the heterogeneity in their audience." (p. 14)

paper_code_entries.value: contingency — dialogue and targeted feedback respond to the creator’s current question or selected draft passage (PDF p. 7).
quotes: "Throughout the process, creators can directly ask personas for feedback on specific sections of their draft (Figure 3 - C)." (p. 7)

paper_code_entries.value: adaptation — the audience-trait overview is generated specifically from each creator’s channel data (PDF p. 5).
quotes: "These data sources allow the system to generate a channel-specific dimension-value set that reflects the unique characteristics and preferences of the audience as shown in Figure 2 - D." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: hybrid_or_multi_model — GPT-4 generates summaries, traits, and profiles while embedding and clustering models organize the audience groups (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Our pipeline generates audience personas with GPT-4 and k-means clustering." (p. 9)
"Using pre-trained BERT embeddings and k-means clustering, the 200 comments are clustered in k groups of predicted audiences." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the semantic pipeline uses GPT-4 (PDF p. 8).
quotes: "The technical pipeline was developed using OpenAI’s gpt-4-1106-preview model." (p. 8)

limitations: "Proxona relies on audience comments to generate personas, which potentially introduces biases." (PDF p. 19)
"Comments represent only a subset of audience behaviors and opinions, excluding non-commenting viewers who may have different preferences or perspectives." (PDF p. 19)
"Plus, the initial step of our pipeline involves filtering comments based on length— which might omit valuable insights from shorter comments, potentially skewing the personas." (PDF p. 19)
"The LLM performance can affect the user experience when handling non-English languages." (PDF p. 19)
"While the Proxona generates data-driven personas, they cannot be mapped to real-world audience populations." (PDF p. 19)
"When there are few or no comments in creators’ channels, the creators may not benefit from Proxona." (PDF p. 19)
"And this under-represents critical, controversial, or dissenting opinions—traits that may be pivotal in creative practices." (PDF p. 18)
boundary_conditions: "While Proxona is intended to support the early-stage creative process, we expect that the improved sensemaking and exploratory processes will positively impact execution performance." (PDF p. 18)
"Proxona is not designed for predictive use cases or guaranteeing specific outcomes, but some creators might expect to earn revenues through view counts, not considering content types." (PDF p. 18)
"Channel activity varied from 1 year to over 6 years (See Table 1)." (PDF p. 13)
"All participants were running their channels in Korean, were aged between their 20s and 40s." (PDF p. 13)

"Our Proxona pipeline, which currently processes transcripts to generate audience persona’s feedback and conversations, can be easily applicable to support other forms of text-based content beyond video storylines." (PDF p. 19)

quotes: "This could be evaluated more directly with a human study, where the design solutions created by subjects prompted by either human or LLM-generated solutions sets are evaluated." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: conceptual engineering design ideation and design-solution evaluation — the paper generates and evaluates early design concepts (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "In this paper, we leverage LLMs to generate solutions for a set of 12 design problems and compare them to a baseline of crowdsourced solutions." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: immediate_performance_or_sensemaking — the support is meant to help designers produce concepts during current design work (PDF p. 9).
quotes: "Our long-term motivation is to support designers during the conceptual design stage by using pre-trained LLMs to generate creative design solutions more quickly and cheaply than current methods, such as crowdsourcing." (p. 9)

paper_code_entries.value: unspecified — the intended users are designers, but the paper does not establish their experience level.
knowledge_or_concept_gap — supplemental concepts complement designers' own domain knowledge during ideation (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Concept generation is a creative step in the conceptual design phase, where designers often turn to brainstorming, mindmapping, or crowdsourcing design ideas to complement their own knowledge of the domain." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: artifact — evaluation concerns the feasibility, novelty, usefulness, similarity, and diversity of generated solution artifacts (PDF p. 1).
quotes: "Expert evaluations indicate that the LLM-generated solutions have higher average feasibility and usefulness while the crowdsourced solutions have more novelty." (p. 1)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — prompts specify output volume, desired attributes, or a worked example, while the rubric and metrics structure evaluation (PDF pp. 4–5).
quotes: "Therefore, the phrase “Generate 100 design solutions for” was attached to the beginning of each design problem, as shown in Figure 1, to enforce GPT-3 to generate 100 design solutions." (p. 4)

"To create the zero-shot prompts, we take the 12 base prompts and modify them to include descriptive adjectives novel, diverse, and unique, to guide GPT-3 to generate solutions different from the base prompt." (p. 5)
"For our task, as shown in Figure 1(c), we append to the base prompt an example of a design solution, and then feed the expanded prompt into the model." (p. 5)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_or_foundation_model — GPT-3 generates the design concepts from problem inputs (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "In this paper, we leverage a pre-trained generative model called GPT-3 to generate design solutions conditioned on inputs of design problems." (p. 3)

paper_code_entries.value: llm_era — the meaning-bearing design outputs are produced by GPT-3 (PDF p. 3).
quotes: "In this paper, we leverage a pre-trained generative model called GPT-3 to generate design solutions conditioned on inputs of design problems." (p. 3)

limitations: "While showing promising results, the methods explored in the current work to generate a synthetic set of inspirational design solutions to a prompt still fall behind established methods, such as crowdsourcing." (p. 9)

"While the human evaluation of individual design solutions from experts proved insightful, there remains a question of the value of the solution sets in providing inspirational stimuli to designers." (p. 9)
"For the computational metrics, future work should verify the effectiveness and validity of the chosen metrics and others in regard to textual design solutions." (p. 9)

"Currently, there exist methods to evaluate diversity, uniqueness, and similarity, but there are no computational methods to evaluate usefulness and feasibility, which currently can only be done through expensive expert evaluations as described in Section 3.4.1." (p. 9)
"Finally, LLMs are still considered a “black box”, and, as mentioned in Section 4.2, their outputs are extremely sensitive to the user’s input." (p. 9)
"A qualitative evaluation of all design solutions used in this work shows that the generated solutions are shorter and contain less information than the crowdsourced solutions." (p. 9)
"Additionally, this paper only examines one LLM, GPT-3, so there still remains a question of whether or not this issue is unique to GPT-3 or ubiquitous amongst all LLMs." (p. 9)
boundary_conditions: "In this paper, we used GPT-3 to generate solutions based on 12 design problems shown in Table 1." (p. 4)
"Additionally, this paper only examines one LLM, GPT-3, so there still remains a question of whether or not this issue is unique to GPT-3 or ubiquitous amongst all LLMs." (p. 9)
